a.d: Monastyr Świętego Nauma (mac. Манастирот „Св.
a.de: One of the most beautiful monasteries in Macedonia and an important pilgrimage place, this monastery is a must-see when visiting Ohrid. Most visitors make this a half-day or full-day trip. With a breathtaking setting on a plateau over Ohrid Lake and Galičica mountain towering from behind, it was fou

The fortress sits like a crown above the old town. It was built in the 10th century when Ohrid was capital of the First Bulgarian Empire by Tsar Samuel, though it was likely built upon foundations of an older fortification dating to the 4th century BC. With its positioning at the top of the Ohrid hi

a.d: Cerkiew Świętych Klemensa i Pantelejmona (mac. Црква Свети Климент и Пантелеjмон) – prawosławna cerkiew w Ochrydzie.
a.de: Situated on the wider archaeological site of Plaošnik, the site has been an important religious centre since early Christian times, if not before. It is the site of the first university in Europe, opened in the 10th century and is the place where the Cyrillic alphabet was created. The church you see

a.d: Starożytny Teatr w Ochrydzie – budowla pochodząca z okresu hellenistycznego, znajduje się w mieście Ochryda w Macedonii Północnej. Został zbudowany w 200 roku p.n.e.
a.de: This is the only Hellenistic theatre remaining in North Macedonia, with the three other ancient theatres being from Roman times. Built in 200 BC, it was discovered by accident in the 1980s. It originally had an upper portion but only the lower portion is preserved. Today, it once again functions as

a.d: Stanowisko archeologiczne i miejsce święte, 250 metrów na południe od twierdzy Samuela. Stoi tu kościół Świętego Klemensa z 893 roku, zbudowany na fundamentach wcześniejszej bazyliki chrześcijańskiej.

Nekropolia z epoki żelaza, z około VII wieku przed Chrystusem, koło północnego brzegu Jeziora Ochrydzkiego. Prawdopodobnie używali jej mieszkańcy iliryjskiego miasta Lychnidos, a w grobach było złoto.

a.n: Institute for Protection of Cultural Monuments and National Museum

a.d: Ruiny kościoła w Lin – znajdujące się w albańskiej miejscowości Lin ruiny kościoła powstałego w VI wieku. W 1973 roku obiekt został wpisany na listę religijnych zabytków kulturowych Albanii.
Starożytna bazylika chrześcijańska i nekropolia koło Ochrydy, przy trasie Ochryda–Struga. Wykopaliska odsłoniły trzyczęściową bazylikę i nekropolię ze 124 grobami z okresu od VI do XII wieku.
a.de: A cave church and ancient Christian basilica right off the A3 highway to Struga. Archaeological excavations suggest the oldest portions of the site date from the 8th century.

a.n: Church of the Theotokos of Zaum

a.d: Średniowieczna cerkiew prawosławna z XIII wieku w Ochrydzie, od XV do XVIII wieku druga katedra arcybiskupa Ochrydy. Grecki napis nad wejściem podaje, że wzniósł ją w 1295 roku bizantyjski arystokrata Progonos Sgouros.
Parafialna cerkiew Macedońskiego Kościoła Prawosławnego we wsi Vevčani, której budowę lub przebudowę rozpoczęto w 1834 roku. Prace zakończono w 1864 roku.

a.n: St. Paraskevi the Venerable Chapel, Vevčani

a.d: Cerkiew Świętej Zofii (mac. Црква Света Софија) – powstała w XI wieku cerkiew w Ochrydzie, jeden z najważniejszych zabytków Macedonii Północnej.
a.de: Dating to the 9th century, Saint Sofia is a cathedral church of the Ohrid Archbishopric. The present church was built during the period from 1035 to 1056. The front façade with the towers and the open galleries was built in 1317 under Archbishop Gregory. The side porch was added when the church was

This church was built and painted in 1295. It is dedicated to the Virgin Mary; "Perivleptos" (from the Greek Περίβλεπτος) is an attribute given to her meaning "the Omniscient and Clairvoyant." The benefactor in its construction was the son-in-law of Byzantine Emperor Andronicus II. The church was pa

a.n: Church of Saints Constantine and Elena
a.de: Built in 1477, this church sits just southeast of Saint Mary Perivleptos. It is a small church with a single nave. The whole interior is painted with frescoes.
Just east of Saint Mary Perivleptos is this 14th century church, dedicated to Saint Demetrius. The three-nave church has high quality frescoes.

a.n: Church of Saints Cosmas and Damian
a.de: Further southeast of Saints Constantine and Elena, is this small church, also built in the 14th century. It has great frescoes, including one which is depicted on the 1,000-denar banknote. It also has a wooden iconostasis.

a.n: Church of Saint John at Kaneo
a.d: Cerkiew Świętego Jana Teologa (mac. Црква „Св.
a.de: This 14th century church is best known for its scenic location, standing on a cliff above Lake Ohrid, likely making it the most photographed of the town's churches. Notable about its architecture is the Armenian influence with the zigzag line of the roof of the dome. There are only a few original fr

Sitting on Plaošnik next to St Pantaleon is a church in ruins, built in the 5th century. It is important as an architectural solution since it has a four-leaf shape. Central solutions like this were built in Syria and Mesopotamia and they became customary much later in Europe, in the 10th century. I

a.n: Church Saint Nicholas Bolnički & Church of Saint Mary Bolnička
a.de: These two small neighbouring churches were built in the 14th century with dormitories around them which were used as quarantine stations for visitors of the city. After the coming of the Turks, they were turned into hospitals. That is where the name "Bolnički" comes from (bolnica means hospital). Sa

a.n: Church of Saint Clement of Ohrid
a.de: This small, well-hidden church, built in the 14th century, is just a few steps away from the Bolnički churches, in the heart of the old town. The church is historically important since it is here that the bones of St. Clement were hidden after the Turks took the city and converted Saint Pantaleon to

a.n: Church of the Holy Mother of God - Čelnica
a.de: This 14th-century church in the old town is notable for being perhaps the only two-nave church in the country. Its oldest frescoes date from the 14th century, but the church was mostly repainted in the 19th century by notable artists from the Debar area.
Built of stone and limestone, this church was completed in 1860. While still not completely painted on the interior, the existing frescoes were done by noted artist Dičo Krstev.

a.n: Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary
a.de: This church, dating to the 17th century, sits just above the main shopping street of the Old Bazaar in the centre of town. Most of the present structure was built in 1832. It has a single dome and contains impressive frescoes. The town's small 16th-century clock tower is nearby.
The Church of Saint Nicholas is in the newer part of town on Partizanska Street, one block north of the lake. It was built in 1863 and has been expanded over the years.
In Ohrid's upper neighborhoods is this 1834-built church. Some of its frescoes date from this period, while its bell tower was built in 1950.
This small church was built in 1965 but looks like it was built centuries ago.

A tekje is a place of spiritual retreat in the Bektashi Order, a type of Sufi Islam. Dating from 1590, the tekje is situated north of the square with the 1,000-year-old tree. It belonged to the Halvet dervish order. The building is square in shape with one minaret. The mausoleum of Muhammad Hayati,
This house was built in the early 19th century and, in 1830, writer Grigor Prličev was born in it. It has served as a museum on the writer's life and work since 2000.

a.d: Zabytkowy dom kupiecki w Ochrydzie, w obecnym kształcie zbudowany w latach 1863–1864 w tradycyjnym stylu osmańskim. Pierwotny dom ukończono w 1827 roku, co potwierdza grecki napis na marmurowej tablicy.
a.de: Hristo Uzunov was born in this house in 1878. He would go on to be the leader of the Internal Macedonian Revolutionary Organization's Ohrid region until his suicide upon being surrounded by Ottoman forces in 1905 near Kičevo. This house was built in the mid-19th century and was owned by the Uzunov f

Within the complex of the Church of Saint Mary Perivleptos, this gallery contains some of the best examples of the iconographic art in North Macedonia. It is considered to be the second-most important and valuable collection of icons in the world after the Moscow collection.

Uncovered in 2009, these ruins are of an early Christian basilica, dating to the 4th or 5th century. The ruins include well-preserved floor mosaics as well as pillars and some walls. The site is situated near the Church of Saint Sophia.

Ohrid's clock tower is less prominent than others in cities like Bitola, Prilep, or Skopje. Nonetheless, it is a historic structure built in 1726. Standing 12 m (39.4 ft) tall, it sits up into the hill under the eastern side of the fortress near the Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary. The t
Established in 1516 making it one of the oldest museums in the world. Now it shows exponents of history, archaeology and ethnology.
Watch paper being made from wood pulp using traditional methods, also copy of the original Gutenberg press. Line drawings and colour prints can be purchased, printed on their own paper.
Excellent photo exhibition(s). Here they provide tourist information, tour guides, maps of the city, and books in English.
This early Ottoman-era mosque is likely Ohrid's oldest, built in 1456. It is located in the city's northwest side toward Struga, and features a pitched roof and a single minaret.
Beautiful mosque with a cross on the minaret.

This 14th-century cave church sits below the village of Šipokno and above the lakefront hotels Sileks, Aura, and Aqualina. The church was built into the natural cave and its frescoes date from the 14th century, though heavily damaged. The elevated position of the cave church gives it nice views over

In a small bay near the Gradište campground and beach, a Neolithic settlement has been reconstructed atop the water along with fortifications and a museum on land. The floating town contains reconstructed prehistoric homes with various objects inside them to help illustrate what life was like at thi

Among Ohrid's most significant churches but not as well known due to its secluded location; the church can be reached only by boat from Trpejca or Ljubaništa villages. Ask around to find someone to take you. It was built on a stunning location among the rocks on a small beach in 1299, while its fres

Immediately next to the monastery is the source of the Black Drim River. This river begins here, flows through the entire lake, and flows back out in Struga, ultimately flowing into Albania past Debar. The springs contain small two islands, one of which is home to a popular restaurant. Tour boats av

a.n: Church of the Dormition of the Virgin Mary
a.de: On the slopes of Galičica is this small 15th-century church. Its frescoes were painted between 1444 and 1451 in a style considered a typical example of church art during Ottoman rule. Its courtyard contains the village's cemetery.

a.d: Duwało (maced. Дувало) – solfatara, jedna z nielicznych pozostałości aktywności wulkanicznej w Macedonii Północnej.
a.de: One of the last traces of volcanic activity in this area, Duvalo is both a fumarole and a mofetta (emitting carbon dioxide and sulfur dioxide). It is often incorrectly referred to as an actual volcano. The smell of sulfur is immediately evident upon entering the village, which sits on the way to Res

a.d: Jezioro słodkowodne o powierzchni 358 kilometrów kwadratowych, podzielone granicą między Albanię i Macedonię Północną. Wraz z otaczającym regionem od 1979 roku figuruje na liście światowego dziedzictwa UNESCO.
Pasmo górskie na granicy Macedonii Północnej i Albanii, między jeziorami Ochrydzkim i Prespańskim. Najwyższy szczyt, Kota, ma 2265 metrów, a na obszarze pasma wydzielono Park Narodowy Galiczica.
Twierdza w starym mieście Ochrydy, stolica Pierwszego Cesarstwa Bułgarskiego za cara Samuela. Według wykopalisk stoi na miejscu fortyfikacji z IV wieku przed Chrystusem, a w 2003 roku ją odnowiono.

Masyw w południowo-wschodniej Albanii, zbudowany niemal w całości z mezozoicznego wapienia. Zbocza są strome, zwłaszcza zachodnie, a grzbiet tworzą rozległe, prawie płaskie powierzchnie z zagłębieniami krasowymi.
Neoklasycystyczna rezydencja w Resen, zbudowana pod koniec XIX wieku przez beja Ahmeda Niyazi Beja. Jej styl jest unikatowy w Macedonii Północnej, a dziś mieści muzeum, galerię i bibliotekę.
Prawosławna cerkiew wzniesiona w 1191 roku, wpisana na macedońską listę informacyjną UNESCO. Wnętrze pokrywają freski w stylu bizantyjskim, a twarze postaci są przepojone smutkiem i żalem.

Solfatara koło wsi Kosel, jedna z nielicznych pozostałości aktywności wulkanicznej w Macedonii Północnej. Z pęknięć w ziemi wydobywa się dwutlenek siarki i węgla, a na początku XX wieku sprzedawano tu siarkę.
Główny meczet Ochrydy i siedziba muftiatu, zbudowany w 1573 roku w Starym Bazarze. Odnowił go wezyr Ali Pasza z Janiny, a jego imię nadano meczetowi w 1823 roku po śmierci wezyra.

Pozostałość dawnych rozległych mokradeł na wschodnim brzegu Jeziora Ochrydzkiego, objęta konwencją ramsarską. To ostatnie duże nadbrzeżne mokradło nad jeziorem i jedno z siedmiu w kraju z reliktowymi zbiorowiskami.
Ruiny kościoła w miejscowości Lin w okręgu Korçë, zabytek kultury Albanii. Podczas wykopalisk odkryto tu mozaiki z IV–V wieku.
Kaplica prawosławna w rejonie źródeł Vevčani, we wnętrzu której znajduje się źródło ze świętą wodą. Potocznie nazywa się ją cerkwią.

a.n: Cerkiew Świętej Barbary i Świętego Savy Jerozolimskiego
a.d: Prawosławna cerkiew cmentarna na małym wzgórzu na północ od wsi Vevčani, w środku dębowego lasu. Kilkusetletnie pnie drzew wskazują na wiek tego sanktuarium.
Cerkiew na wschód od wsi Vevčani, odbudowana po stu latach na fundamentach klasztoru Świętego Jerzego. Klasztor całkowicie zniszczono w powstaniu ochrydzko-debarskim w 1913 roku.

Pasmo o długości około 35 kilometrów, ułożone na granicy Macedonii Północnej i Albanii w formie płaskowyżu. Najwyższym szczytem jest Crn Kamen, 2257 metrów, a na południowym wschodzie leży Jezioro Ochrydzkie.
Góra we wschodniej Albanii, ośrodek Parku Narodowego Shebenik, zbudowana głównie ze skał ultrazasadowych. Występują tu polodowcowe formy rzeźby: doliny, cyrki i jeziora polodowcowe.

a.n: Królewskie grobowce w Selcë e Poshtme
a.d: Iliryjskie kamienne grobowce z III wieku przed Chrystusem we wsi Selcë e Poshtme, na prawym brzegu rzeki Shkumbin. W 1996 roku wpisano je na listę informacyjną UNESCO.
